name: nova.ui.row
signature: nova.ui.row{ count, w, h, gap, y [, x, width] } -> list of { x, y, w, h }
doc: `count` rectangles w by h in a row, `gap` apart, centred across the view (or across `width`, or starting at `x`); `y` is the top (centred when left out).

name: nova.ui.column
signature: nova.ui.column{ count, w, h, gap [, x, y] } -> list of { x, y, w, h }
doc: `count` rectangles w by h in a column, `gap` apart, centred down the view (or from `y`), at `x` (centred when left out).

name: nova.ui.hit
signature: nova.ui.hit(rect) or nova.ui.hit(x, y, w, h) -> boolean
doc: Is the pointer (the mouse, or the first finger) over the rectangle?

name: nova.ui.clicked
doc: Did the pointer go down on the rectangle in this step: a click or a tap?

name: nova.ui.choose
signature: nova.ui.choose{ rects, current [, vertical] } -> chosen, accepted, moved
doc: A choice among rectangles (cards, menu rows) by the d-pad or arrow keys (up and down with `vertical`) or the pointer: moving the pointer over one chooses it; a click on it, or A or start, accepts. `moved` says the choice changed.

name: nova.sprite
doc: Draw an image or one frame of a sprite sheet, centred on x, y, in the world layer. Options: scale, sx, sy, w, h, rotation, color, anchor, frame.

name: nova.rect
doc: Draw a solid rectangle (top-left x, y) in the world layer. color is {r, g, b [, a]}.

name: nova.animator
doc: A small animation state machine for a skinned or animated model. A state is `{ clip = "walk" }` (with `loop = false` to play once, `next = "idle"` for where it goes when it ends, `speed` to play faster, `fade` for its own crossfade time) or `{ blend = "speed", points = { { 0, "idle" }, { 3, "walk" }, { 7, "sprint" } } }`: the two clips nearest the number set with `anim:set("speed", v)` are mixed, their cycles kept in step. Methods: `anim:play(state [, { restart, fade }])` crossfades into a state (nothing if already in it), `anim:update(dt)` once a frame, `anim:draw(x, y, z [, options of nova.model])`, `anim:state()`, `anim:finished()` (a one-shot with nowhere to go has ended), `anim:layers()` (the `layers` for nova.model), `anim.speed` (a multiplier for all of it).

name: nova.model
doc: Draw a 3D model. Options: scale, rx, ry, rz (radians), tint, parts (turn pieces on their own: parts = { wheel = { ry = 1 } }, see nova.model_parts), clip and time (pose it from an animation clip, see nova.model_clips; loop = false holds the last pose), layers = { { clip = "walk", time = t, weight = 0.7 }, { clip = "run", time = t2, weight = 0.3 } } (several clips mixed by weight; nova.animator does the bookkeeping), shadow = false (casts no shadow, see nova.shadows), lod = "cheaper_model" with lod_distance (100) and lod_fade (15% of the distance) metres (draws that model instead past that distance on the ground from the camera, the two trading places by a screen-door so nothing pops; plain models only, not with clip or parts).

name: nova.light
signature: nova.light{ dir = {x, y, z}, color = {r, g, b}, ambient = {r, g, b} }
doc: Sets the sun that lights 3D models: the direction it travels, its colour and the ambient floor. Colours are 0 to 255 multipliers (255 = full). Any field can be left out. Stays until changed.

name: nova.model_colliders
doc: The collision circles made for a model in the model editor (green rings): on the ground in the model's own frame, in metres, x across and z forward. An empty list when it has none.

name: nova.solid
doc: Collision against the triangles of models: hills, caves, cliffs, buildings made in a 3D tool, where nova.walls' boxes and ramps are not enough. A character is a capsule that slides along walls of any angle, walks up gentle slopes (not steep ones), hops small ledges, stays on a slope going down, and bumps its head.

name: nova.solid.add
signature: nova.solid.add(model, x, y, z [, { ry, rx, rz, scale }]) -> triangles added
doc: Makes a placed copy of a model's triangles solid (its whole mesh, as drawn; read from the file the first time). Draw the model yourself with nova.model at the same place. Models with thousands of triangles are fine: they are kept in a grid.

name: nova.solid.move
signature: nova.solid.move(x, y, z, radius, height, dx, dy, dz [, { slope = 50, step = 0.35, snap = 0.3 }]) -> { x, y, z, ground, normal, wall, wall_normal, ceiling, stepped }
doc: Moves a capsule standing with its feet at (x, y, z), `radius` wide and `height` tall (at least twice the radius), by (dx, dy, dz), and says where it ended up. `ground` is true when it stands on something walkable (`normal` is that surface's up); `wall` when it touched a wall or a slope too steep for `slope` degrees (`wall_normal`, with a y above 0 for a steep slope: slide down it); `ceiling` when it hit its head; `stepped` is how far it hopped up a ledge of at most `step` metres. It follows ground down by up to `snap` metres so that it does not leave a slope. Give it the move for one frame (speed times dt, gravity included) and set your vertical speed to 0 when `ground` or `ceiling`; the move goes in short steps so nothing tunnels through a floor.

name: nova.solid.raycast
signature: nova.solid.raycast(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, max) -> distance, nx, ny, nz | nil
doc: The first solid triangle a ray hits within `max` metres: the distance along it (the direction need not be unit length) and the surface's normal, facing the ray; nothing if it hits none.

name: nova.solid.floor_below
signature: nova.solid.floor_below(x, y, z [, max_drop = 50]) -> y, nx, ny, nz | nil
doc: The height of the first solid surface at most `max_drop` metres below a point, and its normal: where a shadow blob or an aim marker goes.

name: nova.solid.count
doc: How many solid triangles there are.

name: nova.solid.clear
doc: Forgets every solid triangle (for a change of level).

name: nova.scenery
doc: The static scenery: trees, road pieces and barriers that never move, kept cheaply and drawn only near the camera (out to `nova.scenery.range` metres if you set it, else to where the fog ends or 300 m; 0 for none; the last 12% of the range fades out instead of vanishing). An entity class with `static = true` and a model puts itself here.

name: nova.scenery.draw
doc: Draws the scenery within `radius` metres of a point. The framework already does this around the camera every frame; call it yourself only with nova.scenery.range = 0, to draw around somewhere else.

name: nova.scenery.add
signature: nova.scenery.add(model, x, y, z [, { ry, scale, tint, shadow, lod, lod_distance }])
doc: Puts a model into the static scenery: pieces that never move. `lod` names a cheaper model drawn instead beyond `lod_distance` metres (100 by default); the two trade places over `lod_fade` metres (15% of the distance by default), each fading by a screen-door, so nothing pops. It is drawn only near the camera and its collision circles block `nova.scenery.push`. A scene file's objects whose entity class has `static = true` do this for you.

name: nova.scenery.ahead
signature: nova.scenery.ahead(x, z, dx, dz, length [, radius]) -> distance, cx, cz, cr | nil
doc: Looks along a line from (x, z) in the direction (dx, dz) for `length` metres, as wide as a circle of `radius`, for the nearest solid circle of the static scenery. Gives how far away it is (0 if touching) and the circle's x, z and radius, or nothing. How a car or a character sees what is coming, to steer round it.

name: nova.scenery.raycast
signature: nova.scenery.raycast(x, z, dx, dz, length) -> distance, hit_x, hit_z, cx, cz, cr | nil
doc: A ray along the ground: the first solid circle of the static scenery it meets (at most `length` metres), with where it hit and the circle.

name: nova.scenery.line_clear
signature: nova.scenery.line_clear(x1, z1, x2, z2 [, radius]) -> boolean
doc: Is the straight line between two points on the ground free of solid scenery? `radius` makes the line that wide. Line of sight, or a clear path.

name: nova.scenery.push
signature: nova.scenery.push(x, z, r) -> dx, dz | nil
doc: A circle of radius r at (x, z): how far to move it to get out of the static scenery's collision circles, or nil when it is free.

name: nova.scenery.clear
doc: Removes everything from the static scenery (a scene does this by itself when it ends).

name: nova.scenery.count
doc: How many pieces the static scenery holds.

name: nova.shadows
doc: Turns on the sun's shadows (set the sun with nova.light). They cover `radius` metres around what the camera looks at: a smaller radius is sharper. `strength` is how dark they are, 0 to 1. Models cast and receive them unless drawn with shadow = false; see-through models never cast. Costs extra drawing, so offer a way to turn it off. `nova.shadows(nil)` turns them off.

name: nova.sky
signature: nova.sky{ top = {r, g, b}, horizon = {r, g, b} [, sun = {x, y, z}, stars = 0..1, clouds = 0..1] }
doc: Paints a sky behind everything in 3D: `horizon` where it meets the ground (and below), blending up to `top` overhead. Colours are 0 to 255, as you would pick them on screen. Stays until changed; `nova.sky(nil)` goes back to the plain clear colour. `sun` is the direction towards the sun: the sky draws a sun there and a moon opposite it. `stars` (0 to 1) is how many stars show, `clouds` (0 to 1) how much of the sky is cloud, drifting slowly.

name: nova.fog
signature: nova.fog{ color = {r, g, b}, near = 40, far = 250 }
doc: Fades 3D models into `color` between `near` and `far` metres from the camera, which hides things popping in at a distance. Use the sky's horizon colour for it to blend in. Stays until changed; `nova.fog(nil)` turns it off.

name: nova.look
signature: nova.look{ toon, outline, exposure, saturation, vignette } | nova.look()
doc: How the picture is treated. `toon = 3` cuts the sun's light into that many flat bands (2 to 8; 0 is smooth); `outline = true` or `{ color = {r, g, b}, strength = 0.85, width = 1 }` draws a line where the distance to the surface jumps (the outline of things; it fades with the fog); `exposure` (1) brightens or darkens through a soft shoulder, `saturation` (1; 0 is grey), `vignette` (0 to 1) darkens the corners. It stays until changed; `nova.look()` clears it. An outline or a colour adjustment makes the world draw through one more pass (about one extra read of the depth per pixel and four for an outline); the toon ramp costs nothing extra.

name: nova.point_light
signature: nova.point_light(x, y, z [, { radius = 10, color = {r, g, b} }])
doc: A light that fades out at `radius`. Call it every frame you want it (it lasts one frame); ask for as many as you like (up to 256 a frame): the 16 nearest the camera, by the edge of their reach, are lit. When the choice changes (you walk down a row of lamps) a light fades in or out over a quarter of a second instead of switching; a light that is new is on at once and one you stop asking for is off at once (a muzzle flash is yours to time). Each lit light costs a little on every lit pixel: a game that needs fewer can use fewer.

name: nova.model_parts
doc: The names of a model's parts (nodes), for `parts = { name = { ry = 1 } }` in nova.model.

name: nova.model_clips
doc: The animation clips a model has, with their length in seconds, for nova.model(..., { clip = name, time = seconds }).

name: nova.camera
signature: nova.camera(ex, ey, ez, tx, ty, tz [, fov])
doc: Set the 3D camera: eye position, target position and field of view in degrees.

name: nova.clear
doc: Set the background colour (0 to 255).

name: nova.view
doc: The size of the screen in logical units (whole numbers, 540 high).

name: nova.time
doc: Seconds since the game started.

name: nova.log
doc: Write a line to the log.

name: nova.ui
doc: Drawing in the UI layer, always at the screen's native resolution.

name: nova.ui.sprite
doc: Like nova.sprite, in the UI layer.

name: nova.ui.rect
doc: Like nova.rect, in the UI layer.

name: nova.ui.text
signature: nova.ui.text(x, y, text [, opts]) -> width, height
doc: Draw text. Options: font, size, color, width (wrap), align, shadow. With `width`, `align` (left, center, right) places the lines inside that width; without it, "center" puts the middle of the text at x and "right" puts its right edge there. Fonts: sans, rounded, pixel, terminal, mono, serif, comic, display, script, or a project font.

name: nova.ui.text_size
doc: Measure text without drawing it.

name: nova.ui.text_width
doc: Width of text in logical units.

name: nova.input
doc: Named input actions. Projects bind actions to keys, buttons, sticks and touch in nova.json.

name: nova.input.down
doc: True while the action is held.

name: nova.input.pressed
doc: True in the one game step after the action went down.

name: nova.input.released
doc: True in the one game step after the action was let go.

name: nova.input.axis
doc: -1 to 1 for axes such as move_x; 0 to 1 for buttons.

name: nova.input.actions
doc: Every action name.

name: nova.input.bind
doc: Change what drives an action. A list of sources makes a button; { negative = {...}, positive = {...} } makes an axis.

name: nova.input.bindings
doc: The sources an action uses.

name: nova.input.reset_bindings
doc: Restore the project's own bindings.

name: nova.input.next_source
doc: The source pressed since you last asked (each press is reported once), such as "key:KeyZ" or "pad:south", or nil. For "press the new key" screens: call it once when you start listening, to drop the press that opened the screen, then every frame.

name: nova.input.pointer
signature: nova.input.pointer() -> { present, x, y, dx, dy, down, right, middle, pressed, released, wheel }
doc: The mouse, or the first finger when there is no mouse, as this step sees it: where it is in the game's own units (as nova.view() measures them), how far it moved since the last step, which buttons are down, whether the main button went down (`pressed`) or up (`released`) since the last step (each once, even on a fast screen), and the wheel. With the mouse locked, dx and dy are how far it was pushed.

name: nova.input.grab_mouse
doc: Locks the cursor to the window and hides it, so that the mouse can turn a camera without end (nova.input.pointer().dx and dy are then the pushes); false frees it. Where the platform cannot, nothing happens.

name: nova.input.rumble
signature: nova.input.rumble(strength, seconds) or nova.input.rumble{ strong, weak, seconds, pad }
doc: Shakes a gamepad for a moment: strength from 0 to 1 (strong is the big motor, weak the small one), up to 5 seconds. `pad` picks the first to fourth pad (0, the default, shakes all). Pads that cannot rumble ignore it, so it is always safe to call. Not wired up on Android yet.

name: nova.input.last_source
doc: The most recently pressed input source, such as key:KeyZ (for rebinding screens).

name: nova.sound
doc: Sound effects (WAV files).

name: nova.sound.play
doc: Play a sound effect. Options: volume, pan, pitch, loop, and limit (at most that many copies of this sound at once: one more makes the oldest copy give way, so a flood of hits cannot steal a voice from other sounds; there are 32 voices in all). `at = {x, y, z}` puts the sound at a place in the world: it is quieter the further the camera is from it (to nothing at `range` metres, 32 by default) and comes from the left or right of where the camera looks; beyond its range a one-shot sound is not played at all (it returns 0).

name: nova.sound.stop
doc: Stop one sound, optionally fading out over fade seconds.

name: nova.sound.set
signature: nova.sound.set(id, { volume, pan, pitch, at, range })
doc: Change a sound that is playing: its volume, pan or pitch (any of them). The change glides over a few milliseconds, so call it every frame to make a looping engine follow the revs. A sound that has ended ignores it. `at = {x, y, z}` (and `range`) makes it follow a place in the world as `play` does: call it every frame for a sound that moves or a camera that does.

name: nova.sound.stop_all
doc: Stop every sound effect.

name: nova.sound.volume
doc: Master volume for effects (0 to 2).

name: nova.music
doc: Background music: one track at a time.

name: nova.music.play
doc: Play music. Loops by default. Options: volume, fade, loop.

name: nova.music.stop
doc: Stop the music, optionally fading out.

name: nova.music.volume
doc: Master volume for music (0 to 2).

name: nova.music.position
doc: How far into the current music track it is, in seconds (nil when no music plays). For a looping track it wraps once the track has played through. It updates every frame, a little behind what you hear.

name: nova.music.seek
doc: Jump the current music to a time in the track. Returns false when no music is playing. A streamed (Ogg) track finds the spot quickly, so even far jumps are heard within a few tens of milliseconds.

name: nova.save
doc: Values kept between runs of the game.

name: nova.save.get
doc: Read a saved value.

name: nova.save.set
doc: Save a number, string, boolean or table of those.

name: nova.save.delete
doc: Forget a saved value.

name: nova.save.keys
doc: Every saved key, sorted.

name: nova.save.flush
doc: Write the save file now (it is also written every few seconds and on exit).

name: nova.start
doc: Hand the frame to the framework and begin with this scene (scenes/<name>.lua).

name: nova.entity
doc: Define an entity class. Spec: sprite, model, tags, depth, hitbox, screen, and default fields.

name: nova.scene
doc: Define a scene class with enter, update, draw, draw_ui and leave methods.

name: nova.goto_scene
doc: Replace the scene at the start of the next frame; extra arguments go to enter().

name: nova.restart_scene
doc: Rebuild the current scene from its file.

name: nova.current_scene
doc: The name of the running scene.

name: nova.spawn
doc: Create an entity from entities/<kind>.lua.

name: nova.particles
doc: A particle emitter. spec: rate (per second), life, speed, size, size_end, color, color_end, gravity, drag, angle, spread, spin, area, image, max, screen, depth. Ranges are {min, max}. In 3D (spec.model = a model name, with a z) y is up and spec.dir / spread aim a cone. Call emitter:burst(n) for a puff, emitter:stop() to stop and let the rest fade.

name: nova.burst
doc: One puff of spec.count (default 12) particles that removes itself afterwards. Same spec as nova.particles.

name: nova.each
doc: Call fn for every living entity with the tag.

name: nova.all
doc: A new list of the living entities with the tag.

name: nova.first
doc: The first living entity with the tag.

name: nova.count
doc: How many living entities have the tag.

name: nova.stats
signature: nova.stats() -> { fps, lua_ms, render_ms, draws, triangles, sprites, memory_kb, entities, scenery }
doc: How the last frame went, for an on-screen profiler: frames a second, what your scripts took and what drawing took (milliseconds), draw calls, triangles and sprites drawn, the scripts' memory (KB), live entities and static scenery pieces.

name: nova.raycast
signature: nova.raycast(x, y, dx, dy, length, tag [, { ignore, height, slope }]) -> entity, distance, hit_x, hit_y | nil
doc: A ray against the entities with `tag` that have a hitbox (circles and boxes); the ground plane is x, y in a flat game and x, z after nova.collision{ plane = "xz" }. Gives the nearest hit, how far along, and where. `ignore` skips an entity (the shooter). In a ground-plane game `height` is where the ray starts and `slope` how much it rises per metre, so a shot passes over a thing whose hitbox has a `height` (and a `base`) that it does not reach.

name: nova.cam3
doc: A ready-made 3D camera: cam3.follow, cam3.first_person, cam3.look, cam3.ray and cam3.ground_point. cam3.yaw and cam3.pitch (radians) say where it looks; yaw 0 looks towards -z, positive turns left.

name: nova.cam3.eye
doc: Where the camera is, as { x, y, z } (set by follow and first_person).

name: nova.cam3.target
doc: What the camera looks at, as { x, y, z } (set by follow and first_person).

name: nova.cam3.follow
signature: nova.cam3.follow(target [, { distance, height, look_height, smooth, fov, dt }])
doc: A camera behind and above `target` (an entity or { x, y, z }), looking at it and easing after it as it moves. distance 9, height 8, look_height 1, smooth 6 (0 stays rigidly behind), fov 60. Turn it with cam3.yaw or cam3.look.

name: nova.cam3.first_person
doc: A camera at `target`'s head (height 1.6, fov 75) looking where cam3.yaw and cam3.pitch say.

name: nova.cam3.look
doc: Turns the camera by some radians (a look stick, a mouse moved); pitch stops short of straight up and down.

name: nova.cam3.forward
doc: The ground direction the camera looks along: what "forward" on a stick should mean.

name: nova.cam3.right
doc: The ground direction to the camera's right.

name: nova.cam3.ray
signature: nova.cam3.ray(x, y) -> ox, oy, oz, dx, dy, dz
doc: The ray from the camera through a point of the screen (in the units nova.view() measures). The middle of the screen is straight ahead.

name: nova.cam3.ground_point
signature: nova.cam3.ground_point(x, y [, height]) -> x, z | nil
doc: Where the ray through a screen point meets the flat plane at `height` (default 0), or nothing when it looks away from it: aiming at the ground under a mouse or a finger.

name: nova.collision
doc: Tells the engine what "the ground" is for collisions, distances and neighbour queries: plane "xy" (a flat game, the default) or "xz" (a 3D game, where y is height); in "xz", `on_collide_<tag>`, `distance_to`, `angle_to`, `move_toward`, `nova.nearest` and `nova.in_radius` use x and z, and a hitbox { r = 1 } is a circle on the ground. `cell` is the size of the squares the broad phase sorts entities into, about the size of the things that collide (metres in 3D). Call it once, early.

name: nova.nearest
doc: The closest entity with the tag.

name: nova.in_radius
signature: nova.in_radius(x, y, radius, tag [, list]) -> list
doc: Entities with the tag within a distance of a point.

name: nova.send
doc: Call a method on one entity, or on every entity with a tag.

name: nova.pause
doc: Freeze entities (the scene and timers keep running), for pause menus.

name: nova.count_alive
doc: How many entities are alive.

name: nova.wait
doc: Inside self:go(): pause the script.

name: nova.wait_until
doc: Inside self:go(): wait until fn() is true.

name: nova.ease
doc: Easing functions for tweens: linear, in_quad, out_quad, in_out_quad, in_cubic, out_cubic, in_out_cubic, out_back, out_bounce.

name: nova.cam
doc: The 2D camera.

name: nova.cam.set
doc: Put the camera's centre at a world point.

name: nova.cam.follow
doc: Follow an entity; lerp 1 locks on, smaller values trail behind.

name: nova.cam.limit
doc: Keep the view inside a world rectangle.

name: nova.cam.position
doc: The camera centre.

name: nova.tilemap
doc: Create a tile grid. Spec: image, tile_width, tile_height, tiles, solid, x, y, depth.

name: nova.solid_at
doc: True when a world point is inside a solid tile.

name: nova.Entity
doc: The base entity class (call nova.Entity.draw(self) from a custom draw).

name: nova.Picture
doc: The built-in picture entity used by scene files.

name: nova.Text
doc: The built-in text entity used by scene files.

name: destroy
doc: Remove the entity.

name: is_alive
doc: False once destroyed.

name: distance_to
doc: Distance to a point or entity.

name: angle_to
doc: Angle to a point or entity.

name: move_toward
doc: Step toward a point; true on arrival.

name: set_velocity
doc: Set vx and vy from an angle and speed.

name: speed
doc: Current speed.

name: overlaps
doc: Whether two entities' hitboxes overlap.

name: touching
doc: The first overlapping entity with the tag.

name: bounds
doc: The entity's hitbox in the world.

name: slide
doc: Move, stopping against solid tiles.

name: play
doc: Play an animation tag of the sprite sheet.

name: play_clip
doc: Play an animation clip of the entity's 3D model. on_clip_end(name) runs when a non-looping clip finishes; set self.clip_speed to scale time.

name: stop_clip
doc: Stop the entity's model animation clip (the model returns to its authored pose).

name: stop_animation
doc: Stop animating.

name: set_frame
doc: Show one frame of the sprite sheet.

name: after
doc: Run fn once later; cancelled if the entity is destroyed.

name: every
doc: Run fn repeatedly.

name: go
doc: Run a script that can nova.wait().

name: tween
doc: Glide fields to new values.

name: draw
doc: Draw the entity (override for custom drawing).

name: nova.noise2
signature: nova.noise2(x, z [, seed, octaves, gain]) -> number
doc: Smooth, repeatable noise from about -1 to 1 for a place on the ground: the same answer every time for the same seed. `octaves` adds finer layers (each twice as fine, `gain` as strong; 0.5 by default).

name: nova.noise3
signature: nova.noise3(x, y, z [, seed, octaves, gain]) -> number
doc: The same noise in three dimensions: for caves, clouds and anything that changes with height.

name: nova.hash
doc: A repeatable random number from 0 up to 1 for a place (whole numbers: the block it is in). Use it instead of math.random when the same place must always give the same answer, like where a tree stands.

name: nova.voxel
doc: A world of blocks, like a block-building game: chunks of 16 x 128 x 16 blocks, lit by the sun and torches, drawn with soft shading, with a ray and a walking box for gameplay. Block (x, y, z) fills x to x+1, y to y+1, z to z+1; y is up. Call `atlas` and `block` once at load, make chunks, then call `draw` every frame after setting the camera.

name: nova.voxel.atlas
doc: The picture all blocks take their faces from: a square PNG of equal square tiles, counted from the top left along each row (tile 0, 1, 2 ...). Call it before any `block`.

name: nova.voxel.block
doc: Defines a kind of block and gives its number (1, 2, 3 ... in order; air is 0). Options: tile (all faces) or top, bottom, side, or tiles = {+x, -x, top, bottom, +z, -z}; solid (a body cannot enter), opaque (hides what is behind and stops light), liquid, shape = "cube" | "cross" (flowers, grass) | "torch", glow (0-15 light it gives), dim (light it swallows: water, leaves), cull_same (no faces between two of them: glass), alpha (0-255, less is see-through).

name: nova.voxel.id
doc: The number of a block by name.

name: nova.voxel.info
signature: nova.voxel.info(block) -> { name, solid, opaque, liquid, glow, shape, tile, side_tile }
doc: What a block is. A block is its number or its name everywhere.

name: nova.voxel.get
doc: The block at a place (air outside the height of the world and in chunks that are not loaded). Positions can be fractions: the block they fall in.

name: nova.voxel.set
doc: Puts a block in without lighting or drawing it: for building a chunk before `finish_chunk`. Use `edit` for changes during play.

name: nova.voxel.edit
doc: Changes a block during play: updates the light, the picture, and what is remembered for saving. False when the chunk is not loaded.

name: nova.voxel.fill
signature: nova.voxel.fill(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, block) -> count
doc: Fills a box (corners included) the way `set` does, quickly.

name: nova.voxel.carve
signature: nova.voxel.carve(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, { through, seed, scale, threshold, kind, squash }) -> count
doc: Digs caves into a box wherever 3D noise says so, but only out of the blocks listed in `through`. kind = "tunnel" (winding passages, the default, threshold around 0.1) or "cavern" (blobs, where noise is above the threshold). `scale` is how stretched the noise is (0.05), `squash` stretches it up and down.

name: nova.voxel.create_chunk
doc: Makes an empty chunk (chunk numbers: x and z divided by 16, rounded down).

name: nova.voxel.finish_chunk
doc: Works out the light of a chunk you have filled with `set`, `fill` and `carve`. It is drawn once it and the eight chunks around it are finished.

name: nova.voxel.has_chunk
doc: Whether the chunk is loaded.

name: nova.voxel.unload_chunk
doc: Forgets a chunk and its picture. Save its edits first.

name: nova.voxel.export_edits
doc: What the player changed in a chunk (by `edit`) as short text to put in a save, or nothing when it is untouched.

name: nova.voxel.import_edits
doc: Puts saved changes back into a chunk after generating it and before `finish_chunk`.

name: nova.voxel.modified_chunks
doc: The loaded chunks that have changes to save.

name: nova.voxel.light
doc: The light at a place, 0 to 15, from the sky and from torches.

name: nova.voxel.top
doc: The height of the highest full block in a column (-1 when there is none).

name: nova.voxel.raycast
signature: nova.voxel.raycast(x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, length [, liquids]) -> bx, by, bz, nx, ny, nz, distance, block | nothing
doc: A ray through the blocks: the first block that is not air (or water, unless `liquids`), the way the face it hit points (nx, ny, nz: to place a block beside it, add that), how far away it was and what it is. Nothing when it hits nothing.

name: nova.voxel.move
signature: nova.voxel.move(x, y, z, half_width, height, dx, dy, dz [, step]) -> x, y, z, hit_x, hit_y, hit_z, on_ground
doc: Moves a standing box (feet at x, y, z) by dx, dy, dz and slides it along the blocks, so a body walks, falls, lands and bumps its head. `step` is how high it climbs without jumping (0.5 is a stair). It says which axes were blocked and whether it is standing on something.

name: nova.voxel.daylight
doc: How bright the sky's light is, 0 (night) to 1 (noon). Torch light is not affected. Set the sky and fog colours yourself.

name: nova.voxel.draw
doc: Draws the world around the camera: `distance` chunks out (6). Chunks are built in pieces 16 blocks high, on worker threads where the device has cores to spare: it hands the nearest pieces that changed to the workers, takes in at most `budget` finished pieces this frame (6) so that the frame rate holds, and without workers builds that many itself. Call it after nova.camera. A piece of the world that has only just been made fades in over `fade` seconds (0.4; 0 for none) by a screen-door, and the last tenth of `distance` fades out, so the world does not pop into view; a piece rebuilt by an edit does not fade again.

name: nova.voxel.cube
signature: nova.voxel.cube(block, x, y, z [, { scale, rx, ry, rz, tint }])
doc: Draws one block as a small cube centred on a place: a dropped item, a block in the hand.

name: nova.voxel.stats
signature: nova.voxel.stats() -> { chunks, meshed, mesh_ms, light_ms, faces, drawn, dirty, threads }
doc: What the voxel world is doing: chunks loaded, pieces built so far and the milliseconds the builders spent (added up over all threads) and the lighting, faces in the last piece, pieces drawn this frame, pieces waiting or being built, and how many worker threads build.

name: nova.clock
doc: A stopwatch that runs in real time (nova.time is game time, which stops when paused). For measuring how long work took, or spending a fixed share of a frame on it: `local t = nova.clock(); while nova.clock() - t < 0.004 do ... end`.

name: nova.voxel.apply_saved
doc: Puts back the changes the player made to this chunk before it was dropped, or that were read by `load_world`. Call it after generating a chunk and before `finish_chunk`.

name: nova.voxel.save_world
doc: Writes every change the player has made (in loaded and dropped chunks) to a file beside the save, written whole and safely. Unlike `nova.save`, it is not limited to 1 MiB (it holds up to 256 MiB): about three bytes for each changed block. `name` is letters, digits, - and _.

name: nova.voxel.load_world
doc: Reads a file written by `save_world` (0 when there is none). Changes come back through `apply_saved` as chunks are made.

name: nova.line3
signature: nova.line3(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2 [, { color, width }])
doc: Draws a straight line in the 3D world, `width` metres across (0.02), always turned to face the camera and lit by nothing: for outlines, aiming beams and debugging. Colour is {r, g, b [, a]}.

name: nova.box3
signature: nova.box3(x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2 [, { color, width }])
doc: Draws the twelve edges of a box with `nova.line3`: the outline of a selected block or a hit box.

name: nova.voxel.threads
doc: How many worker threads build chunk pieces. Without an argument it just says; with one it sets it (0 builds on the game's own thread, at most 8). The default is the device's cores less two, up to three.

name: nova.voxel.terrain
signature: nova.voxel.terrain{ seed, sea_level, base, layers, rivers, temperature, wetness, biomes, beach, seabed, caves, ores, lava, trees, stone, bedrock, water, ice }
doc: Describes the land as data, and the engine makes it, on worker threads where the device has cores to spare. `layers` = { { scale, octaves, gain, amplitude, seed }, ... } raise or lower the ground from `base` (blocks, by amplitude); `rivers` = { scale, octaves, width, depth, seed }; `temperature` and `wetness` = { scale, octaves, seed } are the fields that pick a biome: `biomes` = { { name, temperature = { min, max }, wetness = { min, max }, top, under, ice, trees = { { kind, count } }, plants = { { block, chance } }, cactus = { block, chance, height } }, ... } (the first whose ranges hold wins, the last is used where none does); `beach` and `seabed` = { top, under, depth }; `caves` = { { kind = "tunnel" | "cavern", ymin, ymax, scale, squash, threshold, seed, through = { blocks } } }; `ores` = { { block, tries, ymin, ymax, size } }; `lava` = the same, for pockets in caves; `trees` = { oak = { log, leaves, trunk_min, trunk_max } }. Blocks are by name. A chunk depends only on the recipe and where it is, so it is the same however and whenever it is made.

name: nova.voxel.request_chunk
doc: Asks for a chunk to be made from the terrain recipe (false when it is there or already asked for). It appears in a later frame; `has_chunk` says when. Ask for the nearest first.

name: nova.voxel.pump_chunks
doc: Call once a frame: takes in at most `max` (2) chunks that the workers have made, lights them and puts them in the world, and hands the workers what is wanted. Without workers it makes `max` chunks itself. Returns how many arrived.

name: nova.voxel.pending_chunks
doc: How many chunks have been asked for and have not arrived.

name: nova.voxel.terrain_height
doc: The height of the ground at a column, from the recipe (it does not need the chunk to be there).

name: nova.voxel.terrain_biome
doc: The biome at a column, from the recipe.

name: nova.profile
doc: Turns the script profiler on (clearing what it had) or off. While it is on, every couple of thousand VM instructions it notes which function is running and charges it the time since the last look, so a function is charged for the engine calls (nova.*) it makes too. The scripts run a little slower while it is on. Read the result with nova.profile_report.

name: nova.profile_report
signature: nova.profile_report([top]) -> { total_ms, functions = { { name, ms, share, samples }, ... } }
doc: The functions that took the most script time since nova.profile(true), most first (15 by default): the name and where it is defined, the milliseconds charged to it, its share of the total and the samples. For an on-screen list of what is slow; `nova run --headless --profile` prints the same at the end of a run.

name: nova.input.cursor
doc: A pointer for a gamepad. While it is on, the right stick (or the left with `stick = "left"`) moves a cursor over the screen (`speed` units a second, 700) and A or the right trigger clicks, and `nova.input.pointer()` reports it like a mouse: present, x, y, dx, dy, down, pressed, released, so menus built for a mouse or a finger work on a handheld too (`nova.ui.list`, `nova.ui.choose`, `nova.ui.clicked`). It draws a small cross (`draw = false` to draw your own) while it is in use; moving a real mouse or touching the screen hands the pointer back.

name: nova.ui.list
signature: nova.ui.list{ x, y, count, visible, current, top [, w, h, gap, columns] } -> { current, top, accepted, moved, rows, more_above, more_below, hover }
doc: A scrolling list or grid with the choosing done. Up and down (and left and right when `columns` is more than 1) by the d-pad or arrow keys, the wheel, and the pointer (a mouse, a finger, or the gamepad cursor of nova.input.cursor): hovering chooses, a click accepts; A or start accepts too. `visible` is how many rows show at once; pass back the `current` and `top` it gave last time. `rows` is one rectangle { x, y, w, h, index } for each cell that shows, to draw the items into; `more_above` and `more_below` say whether to draw a scroll hint; `hover` is the item under the pointer.

name: nova.ui.cube
signature: nova.ui.cube(block, x, y, size [, { rx, ry, tint }])
doc: Draws a block into the UI as a small cube seen from above at an angle (an isometric inventory icon), centred on x, y and about `size` units across, in the UI layer: over the UI's rectangles and sprites and under its text. `rx` and `ry` turn it (the default tips it 35 degrees and turns it 45). Use it for blocks whose `nova.voxel.info(block).shape` is "cube"; plants, torches and items are flat pictures (nova.ui.sprite with a frame).

name: nova.input.typed
doc: The characters typed on a keyboard since the last call, in order: printable characters as they are, "\b" for backspace and "\n" for enter. For a name or a number to type in; a handheld has no keyboard, so offer nova.ui.keyboard too.

name: nova.ui.text_field
signature: nova.ui.text_field{ text, max, filter, typed } -> text, done
doc: Typing into a line of text: applies what was typed (nova.input.typed() unless you pass `typed`, for instance from nova.ui.keyboard) to `text` and returns the new text and whether enter was pressed. `max` is how many characters (24), `filter` a Lua pattern each character must match, such as "[%w _%-]". Draw it yourself with nova.ui.text.

name: nova.ui.keyboard
signature: nova.ui.keyboard{ x, y [, w, h, gap, current, upper] } -> { typed, current, upper, keys }
doc: An on-screen keyboard of ten columns for a gamepad, a finger or a mouse (it chooses with nova.ui.list, so the d-pad, arrow keys, the pointer and the pad cursor all work): digits, letters, a few marks, Aa (capitals), space, del and ok. Pass back `current` and `upper`; `typed` is the character of the key just taken ("\b" for del, "\n" for ok; B deletes too), to give to nova.ui.text_field; `keys` is one { x, y, w, h, label, selected } for each key, to draw.

name: nova.walls
doc: Walls for indoor 3D: boxes standing on the ground (x and z, with a height range) that bodies slide along, rays stop at and doors open in. A door is a wall that is switched off while it is open. Rooms and corridors are a list of these; creatures find their way round them with nova.nav.

name: nova.walls.add
signature: nova.walls.add(x0, z0, x1, z1 [, y0, y1]) -> id
doc: Adds a wall: the box from corner (x0, z0) to (x1, z1) on the ground, from height y0 to y1 (0 to 100 when left out). Gives its number, for `enable`.

name: nova.walls.enable
doc: Switches a wall on or off: a door that opens is a wall switched off (call nova.nav.build again when doors change, so that paths know).

name: nova.walls.clear
doc: Removes every wall (and the path grid), for the next level.

name: nova.walls.count
doc: How many walls there are.

name: nova.walls.push
signature: nova.walls.push(x, z, radius [, y, height]) -> dx, dz
doc: How far a round body standing at x, z (feet at y, `height` tall) must move to be out of the walls (0, 0 when it is clear). Add it to the position.

name: nova.walls.move
signature: nova.walls.move(x, z, dx, dz, radius [, y, height]) -> x, z, hit
doc: Moves a round body by dx, dz and slides it along the walls, in steps shorter than the body so that nothing is skipped through a thin wall. Gives the new place and whether a wall was touched.

name: nova.walls.raycast
signature: nova.walls.raycast(x, z, dx, dz, length [, y, slope]) -> distance, nx, nz, id | nothing
doc: A ray along the ground from x, z in the direction dx, dz, starting `y` high (1.5) and rising `slope` for each metre along (0), so that a wall lower than the ray is passed over. The first wall it meets: how far, the way the face it hit points on the ground (0, 0 for a top or bottom), and its number. Nothing when it hits nothing.

name: nova.walls.line_clear
signature: nova.walls.line_clear(x1, z1, x2, z2 [, y1, y2]) -> boolean
doc: Whether nothing stands between two places (each at a height, 1.5 by default): line of sight.

name: nova.nav
doc: Paths over the ground that avoid the walls: a grid built from them, for creatures that must find their way round corners and through open doors.

name: nova.nav.build
signature: nova.nav.build{ x0, z0, x1, z1 [, cell, radius, y, height, ignore] }
doc: Builds the path grid over the part of the ground from (x0, z0) to (x1, z1) from the walls as they are now: cells of `cell` metres (0.5) where a body of `radius` (0.4) and `height` (1.8) standing at height `y` can stand. Call it again when a door opens or shuts. `ignore` is a list of wall numbers to leave out of the grid: doors that something can open, so that a path leads through them (the door itself still stops a body until it is open).

name: nova.nav.path
signature: nova.nav.path(x1, z1, x2, z2) -> { {x, z}, ... } | nil
doc: A way from one place to another round the walls: the corners to turn at, in order, the last one the goal (or the free place nearest it when it is inside a wall), pulled tight so that it has few. nil when there is no way (a door is shut).

name: nova.nav.blocked
doc: Whether a body cannot stand at a place (a wall is too near, or it is off the grid).

name: nova.cuboid
signature: nova.cuboid(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1 [, { color, glow }])
doc: Draws a box between two corners, in the colour given ({r, g, b}); `glow = true` shows it at full colour whatever the light. For walls, floors and lamps made by code: every box is one instance of the same mesh, so a thousand cost little.

name: nova.cuboid_at
signature: nova.cuboid_at(x, y, z, width, height, depth [, { rx, ry, rz, color, glow }])
doc: Draws a box by its middle and its size, turned by rx, ry, rz (radians): the parts of a creature built from boxes.

name: nova.quad3
signature: nova.quad3(x, y, z, nx, ny, nz, size [, { w, h, color }])
doc: Draws a flat square at a place in the world, facing the direction nx, ny, nz, at full colour and a hair off the surface: a bullet hole, a mark on a wall. A colour with an alpha below 255 (`color = { 0, 0, 0, 120 }`) is see-through: drawn blended after the solid things, without hiding what is behind it, as a blob shadow is.

name: nova.bake
doc: Light baked into level geometry: lamps light the boxes of a level once, at load, and the result is one mesh that is drawn every frame at no cost per light.

name: nova.bake.level
signature: nova.bake.level{ boxes, lights [, cell, occlusion, skip_down_at_or_below, skip_up_at_or_above] } -> handle, vertices, ms
doc: Makes a lit mesh of boxes. `boxes` = { { x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, color = {r, g, b} }, ... }; `lights` = { { x, y, z, radius = 12, color = {r, g, b}, power = 1 }, ... }. Each face is cut into squares of `cell` metres (1) and each corner is lit by every lamp that can see it (the walls of nova.walls stop light, so add the walls first, and doors shut), softly by how it faces; `occlusion` (0 to 1, 0.5) darkens corners and the bottoms of walls. Faces against another box are left out, and so are downward faces at or below `skip_down_at_or_below` (a floor's underside) and upward ones at or above `skip_up_at_or_above` (a ceiling's top). Lights that move (a muzzle flash) still light it live on top, with nova.point_light. Gives a handle for `draw` and `free`, how many vertices, and how many milliseconds it took.

name: nova.bake.draw
doc: Draws a baked level for this frame (call it every frame, from draw).

name: nova.bake.free
doc: Drops a baked mesh, for the next level.

name: nova.cam3.basis
doc: The camera's own directions, whatever camera was set last, as { x, y, z } tables of length 1.

name: nova.cam3.to_world
signature: nova.cam3.to_world(lx, ly, lz) -> x, y, z
doc: A place given in the camera's own terms (lx to its right, ly up, lz forward of the camera) as a place in the world: for a weapon or a hand held in front of the eye, or a mark a little ahead.

name: nova.walls.move3
signature: nova.walls.move3(x, y, z, half_width, height, dx, dy, dz [, step]) -> x, y, z, hit_x, hit_y, hit_z, on_ground, ground
doc: Moves a standing body (feet at x, y, z; `half_width` either side; `height` tall) by dx, dy, dz in three dimensions against the walls and ramps: up and down first (so a fall lands and a jump bumps a ceiling), then x and z, sliding along what stops it, climbing anything no higher than `step` (0.5) and staying on a slope as it goes down. Says which axes were stopped, whether it stands on something, and on what: the number of the wall (0 or more) or of a ramp (-1 for ramp 0, -2 for ramp 1, ...), nothing in the air. Add gravity to dy yourself.

name: nova.walls.add_ramp
signature: nova.walls.add_ramp(x0, z0, x1, z1, axis, y_start, y_end [, y_base]) -> id
doc: Adds a slope on the ground from corner (x0, z0) to (x1, z1) that rises along `axis` ("x" or "z") from height y_start at the low coordinate to y_end at the high one (or falls, if y_end is lower), solid down to y_base (the lower of the two by default). A body walks up and down it with nova.walls.move3; its sides and high end are walls. Ramps are counted from 0 in the order they were added; move3 and floor_below name ramp 0 as -1, ramp 1 as -2, and so on, so that a ramp is never taken for a wall. Returns the ramp's own number (0, 1, ...).

name: nova.walls.set_box
signature: nova.walls.set_box(id, x0, z0, x1, z1 [, y0, y1])
doc: Moves a wall to a new place (heights stay unless given): a platform that slides or rises. Move the wall first, then move anything standing on it by the same amount with move3 so that it is carried.

name: nova.walls.floor_below
signature: nova.walls.floor_below(x, y, z [, radius]) -> height, id | nothing
doc: The first thing under a place that is no higher than y: its top, and its number as move3 gives it. For a shadow under a character, or to see where a jump will land. Nothing when there is nothing below.

name: nova.perf
signature: nova.perf() -> { fps, update_ms, lua_ms, render_ms, gpu_ms, frame_p95_ms, frame_max_ms, draws, triangles, culled }
doc: What the engine measured over the last whole second: frames a second, milliseconds spent on the game's update, on its Lua and on recording the frame for the GPU (render_ms; means), the GPU's own time for a recent frame (gpu_ms, 0 where the GPU cannot be timed), the 95th percentile and the worst frame time, and what the last frame drew (draw calls, triangles, and model draws left out for being out of view). Zeros until a second has passed, and in tests. For a game that wants to show or log how it is doing (the stress benchmark) or to turn detail down.
